conviction_note: The mid-quarter guide (FICC slightly softer, 'investment' line much more muted, non-comp up more than $500m, idiosyncratic provisions) was given on 2026-09-16, sold about 4% that day and cut the bar to roughly $13.35. What is left is a lean toward an equities-led beat on a bar that has already been lowered, against a name that sold its two most recent moderate beats (-2.04% Oct-2025, -1.87% Apr-2026). That gives p_up 55 on a 4.3% absolute move, +0.43. The findings sum to +0.9 because the equities finding is sized on its own; the scaled number is smaller because the reaction function on moderate beats is poor.
bar: Q3 2026 diluted EPS about $13.35: TipRanks $13.33 (https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/CH:GS/earnings) and AAII $13.40 from 18 analysts, dated 2026-10-12 (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/514051-what-you-need-to-know-about-the-goldman-sachs-group-incs-q3-earnings). These disagree with Zacks at $12.90 and Hudson Labs/Benzinga at $15.39-16.26 (https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/goldman-sachs-q3-2026-earnings-gs-results-preview). Revenue consensus is $16.87bn (Zacks) to $17.42bn (Hudson Labs). The bar is disputed across providers, so every finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest is 6.65m shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 2.3% of shares outstanding, 2.74 days to cover (equibles.com/stocks/gs/shortinterest, via sweep row, read 2026-10-12). It is not crowded, so there is no squeeze mechanism. The 25-delta skew is -1.78 vol points (calls slightly richer), the put/call OI ratio is 0.83, the priced lean is balanced, and the event-implied move is 3.88%. The stock is down 9.79% over 20 days and 22.6% below its 52-week high of about $1,154.

findings.finding: At the 2026-09-16 Barclays conference Solomon said equities 'continues to be very strong on a relative basis'. Goldman's Q2 2026 equities revenue of $7.42bn (+72% y/y) beat a roughly $5bn street estimate by nearly 50%, and Jefferies' Jun-Aug quarter (reported 2026-09-28) showed record equities, +29%. Against a Q3 2025 equities comp of $3.74bn, the equities line can clear a bar that Morningstar's analyst says assumes the equities boom will 'peak sooner than later'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: equities beat by about 50%, stock +9.0% (2026-07-14). Q1 2026: EPS beat about 10%, stock -1.87%. Q3 2025: beat, stock -2.04% on expenses and headcount. Massive equities beats have been bought; moderate beats have been sold.
findings.why_not_priced: Street equities estimates for Goldman have repeatedly been too low (Q2 2026 actual $7.42bn against about $5bn). The bar was cut after 2026-09-16 (full-year EPS -4.5% in a month per AAII) on the soft parts of the guide, not raised for equities. If the equities strength were priced, estimates would not have fallen and the stock would not have underperformed peers by about 4% on the day of the comment.
findings.independence: Jefferies' fiscal Q3 2026: equities +29% to a record, advisory +25% (https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2998277/jefferies-q3-ib-equities-offset-weak-asset-management-fixed-income). Q2 2026 equities $7.42bn against an estimate of about $5bn (https://pulse2.com/goldman-sachs-posts-record-7-42-billion-in-equities-trading-revenue/).

findings.finding: Tradeweb reported Q3 2026 total ADV +22.4% y/y and September ADV +29% y/y (released 2026-10-06), led by government bonds, rates derivatives and credit. That rates and credit activity is a FICC volume proxy that partly offsets Solomon's 'a little bit softer' FICC and Morningstar's modelled -11% q/q FICC (Q3 2025 FICC comp $3.47bn).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 FICC fell 10% y/y and the stock fell 1.87% despite an EPS beat. Q2 2026 FICC rose 32% inside a broad beat that bought +9%.
findings.why_not_priced: The release came three weeks after Goldman's softer-FICC remark and is an electronic-venue volume series that bank analysts rarely map onto Goldman's FICC. If it were priced, the post-2026-09-16 FICC cuts would have been partly reversed in estimates; AAII shows no upgrades in the last month.
findings.independence: This is a proxy: volume is not revenue, and the company's own statement (FICC softer) points the other way and is sized above it. The September 2026 Fed hike and a 10-year yield near 5% (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/09/22/jpmorgan-chase-falls-3-despite-new-20b-qia-partnership-goldman-sachs-eases-bank-of-america-slips/) imply rates volatility, which is the same transmission and is merged here.

findings.finding: Industry investment-banking evidence is mixed. Dealogic shows global IB revenue in Q3 through 2026-09-15 at $21.19bn against $23.77bn a year earlier (-11%), BofA's CEO guided industry IB fees down about 10%, and LSEG shows Q3 M&A volume -41% q/q. Against that, JPM guided IB fees +mid-to-high teens y/y and Goldman stayed #1 in M&A league tables. Zacks models Goldman IB at $2.76bn (+3.8% y/y on a $2.66bn comp).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: IB fees +55% inside a +9% day. Q3 2025: IB +42% but the stock fell 2.04% on expenses.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The Dealogic and BofA numbers ran in the same Reuters story as Goldman's own guide, and Morningstar had already modelled -12% q/q IB. The residual is that a -10% industry y/y read sits below a +3.8% y/y Goldman IB estimate, so the risk is skewed slightly down on this line.
findings.independence: JPM's Barclays guide points the other way: IB fees and markets +mid-to-high teens (https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-09-15/jpmorgan-expects-investment-banking-trading-shine-third-quarter). LSEG Q3 M&A volume -41% q/q with Goldman #1 (https://www.investmentexecutive.com/?p=116245). The two point in opposite directions, so the finding is sized near zero.

findings.finding: The bar was cut into the print: AAII shows full-year EPS estimates down 4.5% over the last month with one downgrade and no upgrades, Zacks cut Q3 to $12.90 within a week, and the stock is -9.8% over 20 sessions and -22.6% below its 52-week high. Goldman has beaten EPS for 8 consecutive quarters.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After a lowered bar, the moderate beat in Q1 2026 still sold off 1.87%. A cut bar has not by itself bought a positive reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: a low bar is visible to everyone. What remains is that the drawdown was driven by the sector and rates (a 10-year near 5%, a Fed hike) as much as by the company. If the guide were the whole story, the stock would have stabilised after 2026-09-16 rather than falling a further 6%.
findings.independence: 247wallst 2026-09-22 attributes the bank selloff to broad de-risking and rates, with 'no confirmed company-specific catalyst' (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/09/22/jpmorgan-chase-falls-3-despite-new-20b-qia-partnership-goldman-sachs-eases-bank-of-america-slips/).

findings.finding: Guided headwinds land inside the guide: non-comp expenses more than $500m higher sequentially, the 'investment' line much more muted than Q2, and slightly higher provisions on 'a couple of idiosyncratic items'. All were disclosed 2026-09-16 and are in the cut estimates.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: an expense and headcount climb sold a beat, -2.04%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: these were guided. The residual risk is that the unnamed idiosyncratic provisions turn out larger than 'slightly higher', which is the one unquantified item.
findings.independence: Hudson Labs quotes the same remarks (https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/goldman-sachs-q3-2026-earnings-gs-results-preview). It is the same document family, so it counts once.

searched_and_found_nothing: A Goldman-specific cause for the September/October drawdown beyond the 2026-09-16 guide and the rates/sector selloff: none found (247wallst 2026-09-22: no company-specific catalyst).
A borrower or credit blowup behind the 'idiosyncratic' provisions: nothing in 2026 search results.
2026 job-cut or layoff news: only 2022-2023 stories.
Q3 2026 buyback pace or a new authorization: nothing found. The Traders Union 'no new authorization' item is from around the June 2026 stress test and carries no Q3 figure.
Cboe September 2026: on-exchange US equity matched shares -14.7% y/y, index options +22.3%. Mixed and not filed as a separate finding; it tempers finding 1.
Peers reporting before GS: JPM, C and WFC report the same day, BAC and MS the next day, so none lands before this print.

rejected_candidates.detail: The event dates to about June-August 2026 (pages show 06/26 and 08/03) and is long since priced. It is not a Q3 print item, and its Q3 capital-return effect is unknown.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Money365 2026-10-06: Goldman research warns on US government debt servicing costs, stock -1.01%
rejected_candidates.detail: This is a macro research note, not a company result. Its rates content is merged into finding 2's rates transmission.

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly positive and are consistent with the slightly call-rich skew (-1.78) and a cut bar after a -9.8% 20-day run-up. They do not cut against the baseline, which is why the lean is small: the balanced options market already allows for a rebound.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 and the core table: Goldman sold its last two moderate beats (-2.04%, -1.87%), so the equities finding goes from +1.0 to +0.7 and p_up from 56 to 55.
Rule 6: the bar is disputed across providers ($12.90 to $16.26, with only TipRanks and AAII agreeing near $13.35), so all findings stay capped small and print_vs_bar goes from +4 to +3.
Rule 5: the company's own 'FICC softer' outranks the Tradeweb volume proxy, so finding 2 goes from +0.4 to +0.2.
Rule 6 inside-guide: the guided expense, investments and provisions items go from -0.2 toward 0, to -0.1.
The core: the lowered-bar/positioning finding goes from +0.5 to +0.3 because a low bar is visible to all. The IB finding is trimmed from -0.3 to -0.2 because its two sources offset.
Rule 9: no change; the equities finding is already sized net of the guided soft FICC, IB and investments lines.
